title: 2012 HMMT November Theme Problem 4
statement: Find the sum of all real solutions for \(x\) to the equation \(\left(x^{2}+2 x+3\right)^{\left(x^{2}+2 x+3\right)^{\left(x^{2}+2 x+3\right)}}=2012\).

solutions.text: \(\sqrt{-2}\) When \(y=x^{2}+2 x+3\), note that there is a unique real number \(y\) such that \(y^{y^{y}}=2012\) because \(y^{y^{y}}\) is increasing in \(y\). The sum of the real distinct solutions of the equation \(x^{2}+2 x+3=y\) is -2 by Vieta's Formulae as long as \(2^{2}+4(y-3)>0\), which is equivalent to \(y>2\). This is easily seen to be the case; therefore, our answer is -2 .
